salary_negotiation.participant_context:
You have just graduated and are deciding between two job offers.

Your other offer (Company B): $88,000 base salary per year, plus 20 days of paid time off (PTO — paid vacation days you can use each year), and the option to work from home 3 days per week. You can start anytime within the next 6 weeks. It is a smaller company with less room for career growth.

This negotiation (Company A): A more established company with a stronger career track and a shorter commute from where you will be living. Their HR manager will make you a package offer at the start of the conversation. Your goal is to negotiate the best possible package before deciding which offer to accept.

apartment_rent.participant_context:
You have just moved to a new city for work and are deciding between two apartments you have toured.

Your other option (Apartment B): $1,950 per month. Heat and water are included in the rent — you only pay electricity, which runs about $40 per month. Effective cost is roughly $1,990 per month. It is a 20-minute commute from your workplace. The building is older and the unit is a bit smaller.

This negotiation (Apartment A): A newer building 10 minutes from work, with more natural light and a parking spot available. The landlord will present their terms at the start of the conversation. Your goal is to negotiate the best possible deal before deciding which apartment to take.
